findings.summary: TPS2121 current limit is 3.00 A (R12 = 35.7k) and the soft-start cap gives ~38 mA of switchover inrush
findings.description: Equation 2 gives ILM = 65.2 / RILIM^0.861 with RILIM in kohm and a valid range of 18-100 kohm; R12 = 35.7k yields 3.00 A, with the OCP fold-back at 2.4x that. C20 on SS is 0.1 uF; the datasheet's worked example states a 100 nF CSS at 5 V gives 780 V/s, which against the 48.6 uF on ISO_5V is about 38 mA of inrush during switchover. OV1 and OV2 are tied to GND2, which per the truth table means the overvoltage comparators never trip - the intended 'no OV protection' configuration.

datasheet.quote: will provide a slew rate of 780V

findings.summary: TPS2553 per-port limit is 592/649/713 mA min/nom/max with R27-R30 = 40.2k +-1%
findings.description: The datasheet's three current-limit equations (IOSmin = 25230/R^1.016, IOSnom = 23950/R^0.977, IOSmax = 22980/R^0.94, R in kohm) give 592/649/713 mA at 40.2 kohm, inside the recommended 15-232 kohm window. The worst-case minimum of 592 mA clears the 500 mA a USB 2.0 high-power port must deliver, and the maximum of 713 mA stays under the 3.00 A the upstream TPS2121 allows even with all four ports in limit (2.85 A worst case).

findings.summary: ADuM4165 VDD1/VDD2 bypass is exactly 0.1 uF as required - larger values are explicitly called out as harmful
findings.description: C5 on VDD1 and C36 on VDD2 are both 0.1 uF 0603 X7R (CC0603KRX7R9BB104). The datasheet warns that more than 0.1 uF on these internal-LDO outputs can disrupt start-up, so this is a value that must not be 'improved' at layout. VBUS1 (C4, 0.1 uF on VBUS_HOST) and VBUS2 (C35, 0.1 uF on ISO_5V) also match the pin-table requirement, and both supplies sit inside the specified 4.5-5.5 V window.

datasheet.quote: Connect VBUS1 to 4.5 V to 5.5 V

findings.summary: USB2514B-AEZC is the legacy 36-pin QFN order code and is rated 0 C to 85 C; Microchip recommends the 36-pin SQFN for new designs
findings.description: The Product Identification System lists USB2514B-AEZC under '36-Pin QFN (Legacy)' at 0 C to 85 C. The preferred package for new designs is the 36-pin SQFN (/M2 suffix), which is a different footprint. The industrial-temperature drop-in for the same legacy QFN is USB2514Bi-AEZG (-40 C to 85 C). The schematic's footprint (Package_DFN_QFN:QFN-36-1EP_6x6mm_P0.5mm_EP3.7x3.7mm) matches the legacy 6x6 mm QFN, so the MPN and footprint are consistent as drawn.
findings.recommendation: Keep -AEZC for this prototype (in stock at LCSC, C633338/C16251) but record the choice: if sub-0 C operation or long-term availability matter, respin to USB2514Bi-AEZG (same footprint) or to the SQFN /M2 part (new footprint).

findings.summary: Bus-powered ceiling is the host's 500 mA budget, not the magnetics: ISO_5V tops out at ~310 mA against ~235 mA of isolated-side self-draw, leaving ~75 mA for all four downstream ports
findings.description:
Host budget 500 mA x 5 V = 2.50 W; less U1 Side 1 (IDD1(H) 70 mA = 0.35 W) leaves 2.15 W into the converter; at ~90% end-to-end efficiency that is 1.94 W, which at DCDC_RAW ~6.15 V is ~315 mA through the LDO pass element, so ISO_5V tops out at ~310 mA after MIC29302 ground current. Isolated-side self-draw is ~235 mA (ADuM4165 Side 2 IDD2(H) 59 mA typ / 70 mA max, plus U8 feeding the USB2514B at IHCH1 base 70/80 mA + 25 mA per additional active downstream port = up to 155 mA, plus ~3 mA of LEDs). That leaves ~75 mA for all four downstream ports combined. A DCR-based estimate puts DCDC_RAW between 5.8 V and 6.2 V depending on the SS34 forward drop, moving the ceiling to ~310-325 mA - it does not move the conclusion.

The magnetics are NOT the constraint, and the '100 mA' against 750313638 in TI Table 9-3 is not a rating: (1) it sits in the table's application column beside a turns ratio and a size; (2) TI's curves for the electrically identical entry - Figures 6-21/6-22, captioned 'SN6505B + Wurth 760390014, VCC = 5 V', a 1:1.3 5 V -> 5 V '100 mA' row - sweep the load-current axis to 200 mA, while 750313638's own rows carry no figure reference at all; (3) the same part number appears twice in Table 9-3 with two different 'ratings' (1:1.3 for 5 V -> 5 V and 1.3:1 for 5 V -> 3.3 V, both '100 mA'), so the column cannot be a device rating; (4) the LDO column is a headroom fact TI corrected after publication ('Changed LDO from No to Yes for transformer ORDER NO. 750313638'), and this design already has the LDO. Wurth's own thermal curve runs the push-pull output current axis to 1.2 A (~40 K rise at 0.65 A, the same 0.65 A its agency-rated typical-application tables cite as IOut1), and with RDC1 = 0.35 ohm, RDC2 = 0.33 ohm and the SN6505B's 0.25 ohm RON the raw rail still sits at >= 5.49 V at 635 mA.
findings.recommendation: Documentation fix, not a hardware one: the spec's '~700 mA usable / 400-500 mA remains' has been corrected in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-usb-isolator-design.md to the ~310 mA ceiling and ~75 mA downstream figure, and the Known-limitations bullet now reads 'one low-power device'. Do NOT change T1. Bring-up step 4 characterizes the margin (measure ISO_5V current, DCDC_RAW and the host-port draw) rather than deciding a transformer.

computation.result: 2.50 W host - 0.35 W U1 Side 1 = 2.15 W; x0.90 = 1.94 W; /6.15 V = 315 mA; ISO_5V ceiling ~310 mA - 235 mA self-draw = ~75 mA for four ports

findings.summary: U7 CP2 rewired from GND2 to n3A_DET during this review - PR1-low alone did not guarantee the weak-source lockout
findings.description:
As drawn before this review, CP2 was hard-grounded and the only lockout control was PR1 pulled low by Q1. Table 9-3 of the TPS2121 datasheet shows CP2 < VREF and PR1 < VREF selects VCOMP mode, which picks the HIGHER of the two inputs, not IN2. VCOMP is specified 0 / 280 / 600 mV (VIN2 referenced to VIN1), so at the datasheet minimum a 5.0-5.25 V weak brick on IN1 would beat DCDC_5V at 4.85-4.97 V and be selected - exactly the case the lockout exists to prevent. n3A_DET is already high (3.3 V through R9) whenever no 3 A advertisement is present and low when U13/U14 detect one, so wiring CP2 directly to it needs no new parts and gives CP2 >= VREF, PR1 < VREF -> OUT = IN2 unconditionally, and CP2 < VREF, PR1 >= VREF -> OUT = IN1. Control-pin leakage is +-0.1 uA max, a 10 mV drop across the 100 kohm pull-up R9.

Cold-start quadrant (external present, host absent), verified: ISO_3V3 is dead, so R9 is a pull-up to 0 V - a deterministic pulldown on n3A_DET, not a float - and CP2 is unambiguously below VREF. PR1 is unaffected because its R10/R11 divider is fed from EXT_5V, not from the mux output: 5 V x 47k/147k = 1.599 V, above the 1.06 V threshold. Table 9-3 resolves this two ways that agree - row 3 (CP2 < VREF, PR1 >= VREF -> IN1) and row 7 (IN2 <= UV, Invalid Input -> IN1). Once ISO_5V energises U8 and ISO_3V3 rises, row 7 keeps OUT on IN1 until the DC-DC is actually alive. Stable in both directions, no start-up race.

NEW conditional risk surfaced while completing this analysis: CP2's pull-up rail sits DOWNSTREAM of the mux (OUT -> U8 -> ISO_3V3 -> R9 -> CP2), so CP2's logic level depends on the rail the mux is producing. In the combination weak brick present + host present + DC-DC unable to hold its load, that closes a loop: DC-DC sags -> IN2 falls toward the 2.55 V UV falling threshold -> handover to IN1 -> the brick carries the whole board -> if it sags, IN2 recovers unloaded and the mux hands back. The only damping is the TPS2121's own IN2 UVLO hysteresis (2.65 V rising / 2.55 V falling); nothing in the CP2 path adds any. The result is a slow relaxation oscillation (hunting between sources), not a hard failure, and it cannot occur while the DC-DC is within budget or with no external supply attached.

Q1 is on the lockout critical path: the lockout depends on Q1 pulling PR1_SENSE below 1.04 V while sinking the ~34 uA the R10/R11 divider delivers, from a 3.3 V gate drive. Margin is large for any 2N7002 (VGS(th) <= 2.5 V worst case), but the specified MPN's parametrics are NOT verified locally - datasheets/2N7002.pdf is JCET's part while the BOM specifies onsemi 2N7002LT1G. SOT-23 pinout checked and matching; VGS(th) and RDS(on) not.
findings.recommendation: Verify at bring-up: (a) with a Default-USB (non-3 A) source on J2, confirm ISO_5V tracks DCDC_5V and the ST LED stays off; (b) with a 3 A source, confirm switchover to EXT_5V and the ST LED on; (c) cold start on external only - PR1_SENSE ~1.60 V, n3A_DET near 0 V, D4 on, no chatter, then hot-plug the host and confirm a monotonic transition; (d) watch ISO_5V and n3A_DET on a slow sweep for >=30 s with weak brick + host connected to rule out hunting. Mitigation ONLY if the DC-DC proves marginal: re-derive CP2's pull-up from EXT_5V through a divider (upstream of the mux, which opens the loop). Do not implement pre-emptively - it costs two parts and the present wiring is correct in every non-marginal case.

computation.description: PR1 divider level from EXT_5V during cold start
computation.result: 5 V x 47k/147k = 1.599 V > 1.06 V VREF rising; R9 leakage drop 0.1 uA x 100k = 10 mV

findings.summary: MIC29302WU minimum load current is 7 mA; DCDC_5V carries only ~3.1 mA when the mux is running from external power
findings.description: The only permanent loads on DCDC_5V when U7 has selected IN1 are the R3/R4 feedback divider (4.972 V / 40.1 kohm = 124 uA) and the bus-power indicator branch R36 + D6 ((4.972 - 2.1) / 1 kohm = 2.9 mA). Total ~3.1 mA against the 7 mA the datasheet specifies for the MIC2930x family. Below the minimum load, Microchip states the output voltage rises as leakage dominates; a raised DCDC_5V is seen by U7 IN2 (abs max 22 V, so no damage) but would be passed to ISO_5V if the external supply were subsequently removed.
findings.recommendation: Add a bleeder from DCDC_5V to GND2 sized for the shortfall (~680 ohm gives 7.3 mA total, 36 mW) or drop R36 to 470 ohm and scale the feedback divider to 3.01k/1.00k. Provide the bleeder pad at layout as a DNP and populate only if the measured unloaded DCDC_5V exceeds 5.25 V.

findings.summary: SN6505B control pins follow the datasheet exactly: EN tied to VCC, CLK to GND, VCC bypassed with 10 uF + 0.1 uF
findings.description: EN (pin 5) is on VBUS_HOST, the same net as VCC (pin 2) - the datasheet states 'If unused this pin should be tied directly to VCC'. CLK (pin 6) is on GND1; the pin is internally pulled to GND and the device falls back to its internal spread-spectrum oscillator when no valid external clock is seen. C7 (10 uF 0805 X5R 25 V) plus C6 (0.1 uF) bypass VCC against the required 'a 4.7 uF or greater, low ESR capacitor'; at 5 V bias the 25 V X5R part retains roughly 8 uF, still above 4.7 uF.

findings.summary: U8 (AP2112K-3.3, SOT-23-5) dissipates up to ~272 mW feeding the hub, a ~68 C junction rise
findings.description: ISO_3V3 supplies the USB2514B at up to 155 mA (80 mA base + 3 x 25 mA for the additional active downstream ports) plus the two TLV7041 comparators and the strap/divider network. At (5.0 - 3.3) V x 160 mA the LDO burns 272 mW; a SOT-23-5 at roughly 250 C/W puts Tj about 68 C above ambient. Current is well inside the AP2112K's 600 mA rating - the constraint is thermal, not current. This confirms the Task-7 deferred note.

findings.summary: Y2 load caps match Microchip's own worked value: 18 pF gives CL_eff 12.5-13.5 pF against the 12 pF crystal specified
findings.description: Microchip's Figure 7-2 gives C1 = 2 x (CL - C0) - CS1 with C0 set to zero and CS1 = CB + CXTAL; CXTAL is specified at 6 pF, so with 1-3 pF of board capacitance the ideal C1 is 15-17 pF and Note 7-2 states 'Each of these capacitance values is typically around 18 pF'. C32/C33 are 18 pF C0G, giving CL_eff 12.5-13.5 pF against the 12 pF crystal chosen (YXC X322524MOB4SI, 24 MHz, CL 12 pF, +-20 ppm, ESR 50 ohm), a pull of about -15 ppm - far inside the +-350 ppm the hub requires.

findings.summary: Y1 matches the ADuM4165 crystal requirement (24 MHz, <=50 ppm tolerance, CL 8 pF with 8 pF loads) - the same combination as ADI's own evaluation board
findings.description: The datasheet requires <=50 ppm frequency tolerance with <=100 ppm stability and calls for 'a typical crystal capacitance of 10 pF and capacitive loads <10 pF'. C1/C2 are 8 pF C0G, which satisfies the <10 pF load requirement. EVAL-ADuM4165EBZ Table 4 pairs those same 8 pF loads with a 24 MHz, +-50 ppm, 8 pF, 50 ohm 4-SMD crystal (IQD LFXTAL056140REEL), so CL = 8 pF is ADI's own validated point and is what has been specified (SCTF SX3B24.000F0810F30, 24 MHz, CL 8 pF, ESR 30 ohm, -40 to +85 C). The ADuM4165 datasheet does not publish an XI1/XO1 pin capacitance, so CL_eff cannot be computed exactly: with 8 pF loads it lands between 5 pF (2 pF stray) and 8 pF (8 pF stray), a pull error of at most +71 ppm at the low end. LCSC's full parameter set separates the two figures its summary view collapses: the SCTF part is +-10 ppm initial ('normal temperature') frequency tolerance with +-30 ppm stability, against ADI's <=50 ppm tolerance and <=100 ppm stability - so both halves of the requirement are met, and the caveat the first review pass raised is resolved.
findings.recommendation: At bring-up measure the actual 24 MHz frequency at XO1 and adjust C1/C2 if the error exceeds the USB 2.0 budget, staying below the datasheet's 10 pF load-cap ceiling. Tolerance/stability now confirmed (+-10 ppm / +-30 ppm) from LCSC's full parameter set; reading SCTF's own PDF before a production buy is good practice but no longer a pre-fab gap. IQD LFXTAL056140REEL remains the drop-in alternate with published ADI validation.

computation.result: CL_eff 5.0-8.0 pF for Cstray 2-8 pF; worst-case pull +71 ppm
